_comment: SecurityInsight guided install (#225): the questions invardia.com's wizard asks. Keys = the config.json keys Install-SecurityInsight reads. DRAFT 2026-10-03 -- v1 offers container hosting only (VM / Azure Arc install on the machine itself, outside the guided flow). The ONE exception to 'no secrets' is installKey (type secret, #240): Invardia's bundle carries it, never a person; the installer stores it in the install's Key Vault and drops it from everything else. Other secrets are NEVER asked here: the installer prompts for them in Cloud Shell or they are added afterwards to the install's Key Vault. Default names follow <type>-si-<ring>-<edition>-<hosting> (framework 5.5): ring prod, hosting ca (container), edition pro when the install receives a licence (-LicencePath) and community otherwise -- 'defaultByEdition' carries both; 'default' is the Community name.

parameters.label: Subscription for SecurityInsight
parameters.help: SecurityInsight's own resources go here: workspace, storage, Key Vault, container jobs.

parameters.label: Resource group
parameters.help: Created when it does not exist, tagged product, ring, edition, hosting, tenant, owner and purpose. A resource group created in advance by your Azure administrator also works. The default is rg-si-prod-pro-ca when the install receives a SecurityInsight Pro licence.

parameters.label: Owner (the resource group's 'owner' tag, optional)
parameters.help: A team or mailbox that owns this install. Empty = the tag is left empty.

options.label: Azure Container Apps jobs (scale to zero, managed identity)

parameters.label: Microsoft Sentinel / Defender workspace (resource id, optional)
parameters.help: Where your sign-in and security logs are. Risk Analysis reads it. Leave empty when you have none.

parameters.label: AI classification and summaries (Azure OpenAI)
parameters.help: Uses your own Azure OpenAI deployment. The key is entered in Cloud Shell, never here.

parameters.label: Shodan enrichment of public IP addresses
parameters.help: Needs a Shodan API key, entered in Cloud Shell.

parameters.label: The daily pipeline starts at
parameters.help: Collect, Correlate and Deliver run one after the other from this time, every day. The default is 19:00 in the local time of the install's Azure region, after the nightly update at 18:30 in the same time zone (Danish time when the region is not known), so everything is ready by 08:00. A time of your own is read in your time zone below. It stays the same local time all year (summer time included); Operations > Jobs or the setting SI_Pipeline_StartTime changes it later.

parameters.label: Your time zone
parameters.help: Used for a start time of your own. An id such as Europe/Copenhagen, Europe/Oslo or America/New_York. Empty = this machine's time zone (the time zone of the install's Azure region when the machine runs on UTC, as Azure Cloud Shell does).

parameters.label: How SecurityInsight sends its mail

options.label: I use my own SMTP relay

parameters.help: Shared mailbox: SecurityInsight sends as one shared mailbox through Microsoft Graph, as its own managed identity. It may send ONLY as that mailbox (Exchange Online RBAC for Applications); no password is stored anywhere. Creating the mailbox and the Exchange permission needs an Exchange administrator: when you are not one, the install prints the one command for them (setup/Set-SIMail.ps1). Replaces the older setting 'mail' (true = smtp, false = none).

parameters.label: Shared mailbox address
parameters.help: The mailbox SecurityInsight sends as, e.g. securityinsight@contoso.com. Empty = SecurityInsight@<your sign-in domain>.

parameters.label: Create the shared mailbox when it does not exist
parameters.help: Off = the mailbox must exist already. A shared mailbox needs no licence.

parameters.label: SMTP user (empty = anonymous relay)
parameters.help: The password is asked for in the shell and stored in the install's Key Vault (SI-Smtp-Password), never here.

parameters.label: Region for the database
parameters.help: Some regions do not accept new Azure SQL servers; another region in the same geography works.

parameters.label: Entra group that administers the database (object id, optional)
parameters.help: Empty = you (the person running the install) become its administrator; when the install runs as an application (the Invardia Support app), that application does.

options.label: From the internet, behind Entra sign-in (add Conditional Access)

parameters.label: Web app administrators
parameters.help: People (UPNs). You, the person running the install, become the web app's first SuperAdmin and these become Admins. When the install runs as an application (the Invardia Support app), the application cannot sign in to the web app: these people become the SuperAdmins instead, and at least one is required.

parameters.label: Let asset tagging write tags (Defender, Azure, Entra)
parameters.help: Asset tagging runs as its own identity and only REPORTS what it would tag. On = that identity is granted the write permissions (Defender machine tags, Tag Contributor, custom security attributes); the tags are written only once you also switch writing on in the web app.

parameters.label: Update ring
parameters.help: Which release ring this install follows. 3 = broad (default), 2 = early / design partners, 1 = internal test.

parameters.label: ServiceNow instance URL (optional)
parameters.help: Optional CMDB / vulnerability connector. Its credentials are added afterwards in the web app.

parameters.label: Private network: SecurityInsight in your virtual network only
parameters.help: Off (default): SecurityInsight's resources use their public endpoints, protected by Entra sign-in and managed identities. On: the Container Apps environment is created in your virtual network with no public address (the web app is reachable from your network only), the database server, Key Vault, storage and container registry get private endpoints and private DNS zones, and their public endpoints are closed at the end of the install (the registry becomes Premium). Run later setup commands from a machine in that network.

parameters.label: Your virtual network (resource id)
parameters.help: The virtual network SecurityInsight runs in, in the same region as the install. The install needs Network Contributor on it (or on its resource group). Leave it empty and give an address range below instead to let SecurityInsight make its own network.

parameters.label: Or: an address range for SecurityInsight's own network (e.g. 10.212.24.0/24)
parameters.help: Used only when no virtual network is given above: SecurityInsight makes its own spoke network with this range in its resource group (at least a /25; a /24 is the usual size). Its subnets are then the first /26 (the container environment) and the second /26 (the private endpoints), unless given below. Your network team peers it with your hub -- the exact settings are on the hand-off list at the end of the install.

parameters.label: Name of SecurityInsight's own network
parameters.help: Only used when SecurityInsight makes its own network (an address range above, no network id).

parameters.label: Subnet for SecurityInsight's container environment
parameters.help: An empty subnet of at least /27, delegated to Container Apps (Microsoft.App/environments). Created when it is not there (give its address range below); an existing empty subnet is delegated.

parameters.label: Its address range (only when the subnet is created)
Subnet for the private endpoints
parameters.help: Six private endpoints (database, Key Vault, three for storage, registry) take one address each; a /28 is enough. Created when it is not there.

parameters.label: Its address range (only when the subnet is created)
Resource group of your central private DNS zones (optional)
parameters.help: Empty: the privatelink zones are created in SecurityInsight's resource group and linked to your virtual network. Given: the zones there are USED, never created -- a zone missing there is on the network hand-off list for your network team (SecurityInsight never writes a zone into your resource group). The zone of the web app itself always stays in SecurityInsight's resource group.

parameters.label: Your hub virtual network (resource id, optional)
parameters.help: For a hub-and-spoke network: the hub your clients (and your private DNS resolver) resolve through. It may be in another subscription. SecurityInsight writes NOTHING on your hub by default: the id only makes the network hand-off exact -- at the end of the install your network team gets the exact list (peering, DNS zones and records with their addresses, the check to run) and a script it can read or run. Empty: the list is still printed, without the hub's names.

parameters.label: Let SecurityInsight link its web app's DNS zone to the hub
parameters.help: Off (default): your network team links the zone to the hub (or adds its records to your DNS) from the hand-off list. On: SecurityInsight links it itself -- only when a hub is given and the installing identity may join the hub network (Network Contributor on the hub virtual network); the right is checked before any change, and without it nothing is written in the hub and the step stays on the hand-off list.

parameters.label: Let SecurityInsight peer its network with the hub (needs your network team's approval)
parameters.help: Off (default): the peering is on the hand-off list for your network team, with its exact settings. On: SecurityInsight makes the peering in BOTH directions and waits until both read Connected -- only when a hub is given and the installing identity has Network Contributor on both virtual networks (checked before any change). Never half a peering: when the second side cannot be made, the first is removed again.

parameters.label: Encrypt with your own key (customer-managed keys)
parameters.help: Off (default): Microsoft-managed keys. On: the Pro database (Transparent Data Encryption), the storage account and -- when chosen below -- Log Analytics are encrypted with a key in your Key Vault, rotated automatically every year. The vault gets purge protection (Azure requires it; it cannot be turned off again).

parameters.label: Key Vault that holds the key (resource id, optional)
parameters.help: Empty: SecurityInsight's own Key Vault.

parameters.label: Key name
parameters.help: Used as it is when it is there (an RSA key); created when it is not (RSA 3072, rotated every year).

parameters.label: Log Analytics with your key

options.label: No -- Log Analytics keeps Microsoft-managed keys
Yes -- link to my existing dedicated Log Analytics cluster
Yes -- create a dedicated cluster (a commitment of 100 GB a day)

parameters.help: Log Analytics takes a customer-managed key only through a dedicated cluster. Data from before the link keeps Microsoft's keys.

parameters.label: Invardia Support app (client id, optional)
parameters.help: The 'Invardia Support for SecurityInsight - PIM Manager (customer request-based only)' app in your tenant. Pre-filled from your support environment. Empty = no support access is granted.

options.label: Troubleshoot: read the Pro database and Key Vault names, own SecurityInsight's app registrations
Setup: also manage Key Vault secrets and administer the Pro database

parameters.label: Invardia install key
parameters.help: Filled in by your installation page, never typed. SecurityInsight Pro uses it to fetch its updates from Invardia (and it identifies the install's telemetry). The install stores it only in the install's Key Vault (SI-Invardia-InstallKey); it is never shown, never logged and never written to SecurityInsight's configuration. Empty = the install claims its own key with its licence.

requiredRights: Contributor + Role Based Access Control Administrator on the resource group (or Owner on the subscription, to create it)

Owner or User Access Administrator on what SecurityInsight reads (the subscription, management group or tenant root) and on the Sentinel/Defender workspace -- only to grant read access to SecurityInsight's identity; the install hands this one command to someone who has it

Privileged Role Administrator (or Global Administrator) -- only to grant SecurityInsight's identity its read-only Microsoft Graph and Defender permissions; the install hands this one command to someone who has it

Resource providers registered on the subscription (Microsoft.App, Microsoft.OperationalInsights, Microsoft.Insights, Microsoft.ContainerRegistry, Microsoft.ManagedIdentity, Microsoft.KeyVault, Microsoft.Storage; Pro: Microsoft.Sql) -- Contributor on the subscription registers them
costStatement: Estimate, small to medium tenant: Community about 10-20 USD a month (Container Apps jobs scale to zero, container registry Basic, storage, Key Vault) plus Log Analytics ingestion, which grows with the number of assets. Pro adds the database (about 5-15 USD) and the web app (about 10-25 USD, scales to zero).
